name: renovatelint
one_liner: Static linter for Renovate bot config files (renovate.json / .renovaterc.json / renovate key in package.json) - flags twelve shape defects enabling supply-chain, unguarded-automerge, and credential-leak attacks against Renovate-managed dependency updates.
problem: Renovate is the dominant open-source dependency-update bot (reported as covering 90+ package managers in 2026), and its config file is a developer-authored artifact that lives on disk and governs when and how dependency updates auto-merge. The October 21 2026 LiteLLM supply-chain attack (Help Net Security 2026-10-22, Socket 2026-10, SOCRadar 2026-10, Aviatrix 2026-10) escalated the fault class the config can prevent: attackers pushed a trojanized wheel (LiteLLM 1.107.0) through the official pipeline and roughly 49,000 installs harvested AWS / Azure / GCP / Kubernetes credentials, AI provider secrets, and developer keys in the ~104-minute exposure window before yank. The 2026 Renovate security-mode posture (Compass Security 2026-05, safeguard.sh 2026-10, systemshardening.com 2026) names the shape family explicitly: a 14-day minimumReleaseAge quarantine would have let the registry yank the malicious wheel before any Renovate PR auto-merged. renovatelint flags twelve shape defects on a 5 HIGH / 5 MEDIUM / 2 INFO split: RNV-001 enabled:false silently disables the config (stealth-off); RNV-002 root automerge:true with no minimumReleaseAge quarantine (unguarded auto-merge, direct LiteLLM mitigation); RNV-003 extends preset references a repo preset without a #<tag> or @<40-hex-SHA> pin (mutable supply-chain source); RNV-004 credential-shaped literal (JWT / AWS / GitHub token / PEM / bearer) inlined under hostRules / token / env fields; RNV-005 allowedPostUpgradeCommands entry pipes a network fetch into a shell interpreter (fetch-and-exec supply-chain shape); RNV-006 hidden-character class (Plane 14 TAG, bidi overrides, zero-width, mid-string BOM, control, PUA) in any string value; RNV-007 packageRules entry has automerge:true without matchUpdateTypes to narrow scope (over-broad auto-merge including major); RNV-008 vulnerabilityAlerts.enabled:false or osvVulnerabilityAlerts:false (silently drops vulnerability-driven PRs); RNV-009 allowedPostUpgradeCommands has non-empty entries (execution surface present, review required); RNV-010 minimumReleaseAge set but shorter than 7 days (quarantine window below the 2026 industry recommendation); RNV-011 missing $schema reference (no editor validation surface); RNV-012 missing timezone field (cross-TZ schedule drift). Independent implementation, not affiliated with or endorsed by Mend / Renovate, the Renovate maintainer community, or any of the cited security publications.
clean_room: Rules are derived from the public Renovate documentation (https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/ and https://docs.renovatebot.com/presets-config/) and the public 2026 security-mode community posture (Compass Security 2025-05 renovate-keeping-your-updates-secure; safeguard.sh 2026 renovate-2026-security-mode-field-test; systemshardening.com Renovate and Dependabot Security Configuration), together with public coverage of the October 21 2026 LiteLLM supply-chain attack (Help Net Security 2026-10-22, Socket 2026-10, SOCRadar 2026-10, Aviatrix 2026-10). No Mend- or community-published linter reference implementation was read, vendored, or mirrored. Rule semantics are shape-only: a renovate config file is a developer-authored artifact on disk; shape defects at that layer are detectable statically.
